title: Schedule a visit for a pet
asserts: Booking a visit (no vet in this scenario) via the real HTTP API succeeds and is listed.
surfaces: Functional / RestAssured against a running server
notes: Pre-existing baseline scenario; does not touch the vet field.

title: Edit a visit description
asserts: Renaming a visit (no vet involved) persists the new description.
surfaces: Functional / RestAssured against a running server
notes: Flagged 'modified' by the manifest but byte-identical to origin/main; only a new scenario was appended after it in the file.

title: Renaming a visit leaves the vet who attended it alone
asserts: A visit created with a vet already attached keeps that vet after an edit that only changes the description.
surfaces: Functional / RestAssured against a running server
notes: #37: guards the exact regression the ticket names for pet types (s5). Note: the step iUpdateVisitDescription() itself reads the vet back off a prior GET and resends it — this proves a correctly-behaving client preserves the vet across a PUT, not that the server does so on its own (the server's PUT is a full replace; omitting vetId clears it, per update_withoutVet_clearsTheOneOnFile). Whether the real Angular edit form is such a correctly-behaving client is inferred from its template, not covered by any test.
